introduction: This level shifts from straight lines to planes (two dimensions). It introduces Projectile Motion and applies Newton's Laws to more complex systems like Atwood machines (pulleys), inclined planes, and systems involving friction.

core_concepts.title: Projectile Motion
core_concepts.description: Motion in two dimensions under constant gravitational acceleration. The horizontal velocity remains constant (a=0), while the vertical motion behaves like 1D free-fall.

core_concepts.title: Static vs. Kinetic Friction
core_concepts.description: Static friction is a self-adjusting force that prevents motion up to a maximum limit (Limiting Friction = μ_s * N). Kinetic friction acts when the object is sliding and is generally constant (f_k = μ_k * N).

core_concepts.title: Motion on an Inclined Plane
core_concepts.description: Gravity must be resolved into components: mg*sin(θ) pulls the object down the incline, and mg*cos(θ) acts perpendicular to the incline, balancing the Normal force.

core_concepts.title: Pulley Systems (Atwood Machine)
core_concepts.description: In an ideal massless and frictionless string/pulley system, the tension (T) is uniform throughout the string. The common acceleration is (Net Pulling Force) / (Total Mass).

core_concepts.title: Uniform Circular Motion Basics
core_concepts.description: Even when moving at a constant speed in a circle, velocity changes due to direction. This requires a centripetal force directed toward the center (F = mv^2 / r).

important_entities.name: Coefficient of Friction (μ)
important_entities.significance: Determines the roughness between two specific surfaces in contact. μ_s is always slightly greater than μ_k.

important_entities.name: Angle of Repose
important_entities.significance: The maximum angle of an inclined plane at which a resting body remains in equilibrium without sliding down.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A common mistake is assuming N = mg. If a body is on an incline, N = mg*cos(θ). If you press down on a block, N = mg + F. Always calculate N from the FBD by balancing perpendicular forces.
Friction is only μN when it is limiting (about to slide) or kinetic (already sliding). If you apply 2N of force to a block that requires 10N to move, the static friction is merely 2N, not 10N.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: θ and (90-θ) hit the same spot
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: For a given initial velocity, throwing a projectile at 30 degrees and 60 degrees will yield the exact same horizontal Range. Maximum range occurs at 45 degrees.

exam_strategy_tips: For JEE Main, master 'connected bodies' shortcuts: Common Acceleration = (Unbalanced driving force) / (Total mass).
In projectile problems, treat the X-axis and Y-axis as entirely separate problems connected only by 'Time (t)'.
